stages.flavor: A sturdy calf with clover sprouting along its spine, raised on the terraced fields around Żebbuġ. Farmers say a field it has slept in never fails.
stages.name: Calfleaf

stages.flavor: Its horns have grown into gnarled carob and fig vines. After the winter storms it shoulders the fallen rubble walls back into place.
stages.name: Vinehorn

stages.flavor: A great moss-backed bull as old as the temple stones. It charges with the weight of a megalith, and the builders of Ġgantija are said to have raised their walls on its strength.
stages.name: Moss-taur

stages.flavor: A rabbit-hound pup with an ember glowing at the tip of its tail. Like the island's own hounds, its ears blush red when it gets excited.
stages.name: Pharawoof

stages.flavor: Its ears burn with a steady flame that sees further than its eyes. Phoenician traders believed it could smell a storm three days before it broke.
stages.name: Infernux

stages.flavor: A tall, gilded hound that reads what is coming in the flicker of its own fire. The oracles at Tas-Silġ kept one beside the altar.
stages.name: Pyrollis

stages.flavor: A round little duck that paddles the saltpans at dawn, nibbling brine shrimp and scolding the fishermen.
stages.name: Duckling

stages.flavor: A broad-billed swimmer that rides the harbour swell like a painted luzzu, steering with its flat tail.
stages.name: Platyflow

stages.flavor: Its feathers have hardened into a plated hull with a ram at the bill, like the galleys of the Knights. It keeps watch over the mouth of the Grand Harbour.
stages.name: Marinedge
